source: NZ Bay of Plenty BoP 25m DTM
compiled_from: Multibeam and single-beam survey data from NIWA and LINZ, plus international surveys (USA, Germany vessels). Cites Lamarche et al. 2018 as the underlying compilation.
obtained_via: ArcGIS ImageServer exportImage request, keyless, no auth required
output_crs: EPSG:4326 (reprojected on the fly by the ImageServer at export time)
units: metres, negative = below sea level (bathymetry), positive = elevation (topography). Combined DTM, not chart datum — vertical reference is approximately MSL, not LAT.

value_range_observed.note: full bbox includes open Bay of Plenty water outside the harbour mouth, hence depths beyond harbour-channel scale

licence: NIWA Open Data Licence BY-NN-NC-SA v1 (https://niwa.co.nz/environmental-information/licences/niwa-open-data-licence-by-nn-nc-sa-version-1) — attribution required, NON-COMMERCIAL, share-alike, no additional restrictions beyond those. IMPORTANT: confirm this licence is compatible with how TideMap is distributed (e.g. an installable iPad artwork) before shipping it — NC/SA terms may need Ryan's sign-off if the piece is ever sold or the licence's exact text differs from this summary (page returned 404 on fetch, summary is from search-result excerpts, verify directly).
notes: This is the best real, keyless, resolution-appropriate bathymetry obtained this round: 25 m grid, ~18x finer than the GEBCO fallback, and it does show real channel-scale depth gradients (validated: a transect sampled at 40px spacing crosses from +20 m land through 0 and down to -46 m, a plausible harbour-mouth-to-shelf profile, not a flat/degenerate raster).

Still coarser than what LINZ layer 122679 (Bay of Plenty Multibeam 2m Depth Model, 2024/25, LAT datum) would give inside the harbour itself — that layer needs an LDS key. See research/overnight-2026-07-27/bathy/README.md for the full comparison and recommendation.

Vertical datum is NOT tide/chart datum (LAT) — do not blend directly with the renderer's drying-height raster (which is tide-referenced) without a datum offset; treat this as a shape/relief source, not an absolute-depth source, until reconciled.
